text: Everything in this course so far has been explained one concept at a time. On the job, it all happens at once, on one request, in one week. This lesson walks through a single fictional project from a business request to production, so you can see how everything connects — and gives you the same project to practice yourself.

You're the newest member of the data team at Castlebridge Retail. Your sales director emails: our regional managers keep asking me for last month's numbers, I need a dashboard that shows revenue by region and by product category, updated automatically, so they can check it themselves. That's a real request, written the way real requests arrive — informal, a little vague, and missing details you'll have to ask about or make a judgment call on.

Your checklist: write user stories breaking that one paragraph into real backlog items with acceptance criteria; build a Kanban board and move your top priority into To Do; simulate Build and Test with a QA plan covering at least one edge case; simulate UAT by writing a sign-off in the sales director's own voice; write short, specific release notes; and respond to a simulated production incident two days after launch.

A student who's only studied the technology in isolation can usually write the query. A student who's also done this exercise can say, in an interview, exactly how that query's result becomes a backlog item, gets reviewed, tested, signed off by the business, and gets released — and what they'd do when it breaks two days later. That's the difference between knowing the technology and being ready for the job around it.
